english.title: Holder of manufacturing authorisation fail to put in place arrangements to enable qualified person to carry out duties

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials Regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the holder of a manufacturing authorisation, failed to put and keep in place arrangements which would have enabled the qualified person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE QUALIFIED PERSON..), to carry out

(A)_[his]_
(B)_[her]_

duties, including placing at

(C)_[his]_
(D)_[her]_

disposal all the necessary facilities
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 42(d), 49(1)(l) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 49 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 makes a breach of reg 42 an offence.
(ii) Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides that a person does not commit an offence under these Regulations if he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid the commission of that offence. Where evidence is adduced which is sufficient to raise an issue with respect to that defence, the court or jury shall assume that the defence is satisfied unless the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that it is not.
